whyItPrints: Missed-call recovery is a dull job local shops already pay for. They pay monthly so a lead does not disappear when nobody picks up.
whyThisMatters:
A roofer is on a roof. The phone rings. Nobody picks up, and the caller dials the next name. Magnetic Funnels is the thing that answers. It texts back in the shop's name, asks what they need, offers real times from the calendar, and books the job. You keep your old phone number. If the caller asks something it does not know, it takes a name and texts you.

The team is in Bettendorf, Iowa. They set this up for heating, plumbing, roofing, remodeling, med spas, restaurants, and similar shops across the US. The same system can send review requests after a job, and email or text old customers. There is no long contract. The site says more than 270 accounts are active. The Stripe count of subscriptions is a bit lower than that, so I am not treating those as the same number.

You pay so a missed call still becomes a job on the calendar.
